submission.justification: Recommend Algorithm-L2 at a 40 GeV threshold. Among the evaluated candidate/threshold points within the allowed 20–60 GeV range, this gives the highest recorded signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate: 93.175%, exceeding the best recorded efficiencies for Algorithm-L1 (85.261% at 40 GeV coarse; 85.996% at 36 GeV fine) and Algorithm-L3 (74.691% at 35 GeV coarse; 74.393% at 37 GeV fine). A fine scan around L2 found 92.421% at 41 GeV, but the recorded overall best remains the coarse 40 GeV point at 93.175%.

requirements.requirement: Use one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md.
requirements.evidence: The selected option is Algorithm-L2, one of the three candidate algorithms evaluated: Algorithm-L1, Algorithm-L2, and Algorithm-L3.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us.
requirements.evidence: Recorded screening flags show latency_eligible_Algorithm_L2 = 1 and recommended_latency_requirement_pass = 1. The numeric latency fields were not documented in the recorded results (latency_us_Algorithm_L2 = -1; latency_documented_count = 0), so this acceptance relies on the recorded eligibility/pass flags rather than an explicit latency value.

requirements.requirement: Threshold must be between 20 and 60 GeV.
requirements.evidence: The recommended threshold is 40 GeV, and recommended_threshold_in_range = 1.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate.
requirements.evidence: At allocated_rate_khz = 8, the recorded best overall evaluated point is Algorithm-L2 at 40 GeV with efficiency 93.175% (fine_best_overall_with_coarse_algorithm_code = 2, threshold = 40, efficiency = 93.175; recommended_efficiency_pct = 93.175).

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended algorithm and threshold.
requirements.evidence: Submitted one recommendation: Algorithm-L2 with a 40 GeV threshold.
